classification.difficultyReason: Find a side, then an obtuse angle, and reconcile the sine-rule supplement with the cosine-rule result.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8, below stem and before part a
spec.description: Elongated blue triangle with left, upper-right and lower-right vertices. Black side labels lie outside the triangle: 13 above the upper edge, 7 right of the right edge, italic x below the lower edge. Interior labels 30 degrees at upper-right and alpha at lower-right have no visible arcs. No vertex names or right-angle marks.
spec.mathematics: Sides 13 and 7 enclose 30 degrees; x is opposite 30 degrees. Alpha is between x and 7, opposite 13. Preserve schematic source orientation.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find $x$ using cosine rule to 4 d.p.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence find $\alpha$ to 2 d.p using cosine rule.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use sine rule to find $\alpha$ to check your answer.

answer.worked:
Use the unrounded value of $x$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin\alpha}{13}&=\frac{\sin30^\circ}{x}\\[8pt]\phi&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{13\sin30^\circ}{x}\right)\end{align*}$$
$\alpha$ is obtuse from part b, so take the supplement of the acute angle $\phi$.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=180^\circ-\phi\\[8pt]\alpha&\approx123.23^\circ\end{align*}$$
